candidates.root_cause: Chamber pressure CV, RF self-bias range, and susceptor rotation delta excursions in EQ_39A6BA_CH04 during operation 5000 (dielectric deposition) caused non-uniform plasma energy distribution and mechanical stress transfer, leading to microcrack formation (K24/P07), wafer bow change, and CONTACT_RETRY electrical failures.
candidates.causal_explanation: The observed +11.4% chamber_pressure_cv, +18.5% rf_self_bias_range, and +8.1% susceptor_rotation_delta indicate instability in plasma ignition, power coupling, and thermal/mechanical uniformity during CVD. This disrupts film stress evolution and interfacial adhesion, producing INCIDENT_OBSERVATION crack length density excursions and POST_CVD_STRESS_PROXY wafer bow change. These physical changes propagate to downstream electrical test as CONTACT_RETRY — a known failure mode linked to microcrack-induced via/contact integrity loss — and manifest spatially as K24 defects with P07 pattern dominance.

distinguishing_predictions.prediction: K24 defects will be observed in RCP_E5F5B889 lots but not in RCP_184CE7C6 lots exposed to the same chamber excursion window.
